Expressivity & formal languages · 2024

What Formal Languages Can Transformers Express? A Survey

Lena Strobl, William Merrill, Gail Weiss, David Chiang, and Dana Angluin

A map of expressivity results—and the assumptions that make them fit together.

Read the paper ↗Companion video ↓

The idea, briefly

The survey organizes theoretical work on which formal languages transformers can recognize. It documents the assumptions behind different results and provides a framework for comparing findings that can initially seem contradictory.

For a reader moving between papers, this is an entry point into the vocabulary of the area: what a result says depends on which transformer model it studies.

Editorial overview based on the paper’s abstract. Reading suggestions below are editorial guidance.

Why spend time here?

For reading two apparently contradictory results and figuring out which assumptions changed.

A way into the paper

  • Start with the definitions of the computational models before comparing their language classes.
  • Use the references to follow one expressivity question into its original proofs.
Keep in mind

A survey is a map of the literature at its publication date. Check the original paper for the exact statement and assumptions of any theorem you plan to use.
